vulnerabilities.description: Insecure file permissions on memory storage. writeFileSync() uses default umask creating world-readable files. Sensitive session data, tokens, or authentication context stored here could be exposed to other system users.
Insecure file permissions on session files. Session data written with default permissions allowing other system users to read session context, metrics, and timestamps. Should use 0o600 mode.

Unsafe external command in deployment script. Uses `curl -s ifconfig.me` to determine VPS IP without verification. If compromised, could redirect to wrong IP. Recommend using `hostname -I` or AWS metadata service instead.
Wildcard server_name configuration allows Host header spoofing. Uses `server_name _;` which accepts requests for any hostname, bypassing DNS pinning. Configure explicit domain names once available.
Missing input validation on keys. Although keys aren't used in paths, untrusted keys could overwrite sensitive memory entries. Should validate key format (alphanumeric + underscore only).

Temp file creation could be improved. Current implementation uses 8 bytes randomness (256-bit entropy) which is cryptographically sound, but Node's fs.mkdtemp() provides guaranteed atomicity. Also, temp cleanup could fail silently in edge cases.
Silent corruption recovery masks potential tampering or data loss. Session restore catches JSON parse errors and starts fresh without logging. Recommend audit logging for corruption events.
Missing HTTPS/TLS configuration. HTTP-only serving allows man-in-the-middle attacks. Configure SSL certificates (Let's Encrypt recommended) and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
Missing security headers. No X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, or Content-Security-Policy headers configured. Adds unnecessary XSS/clickjacking risk.

Deploy script runs with root privileges without input validation. No verification of file paths or checksums before deployment. Recommend adding integrity checks and non-root deployment where possible.

recommendations: CRITICAL: Add explicit file permissions to memory.js and session.js using mode 0o600 (owner read/write only) to prevent information disclosure to other system users.
CRITICAL: Configure HTTPS/TLS in nginx.conf using Let's Encrypt SSL certificates and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
HIGH: Replace wildcard server_name with explicit domain configuration (server_name valleyofthesunmoving.com www.valleyofthesunmoving.com;) to prevent Host header spoofing.
HIGH: Add security headers to nginx.conf: X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block, Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'
MEDIUM: Use Node's fs.mkdtemp() instead of tmpdir() + randomBytes in github-safe.js for guaranteed TOCTOU safety in temp file creation.
MEDIUM: Improve deploy.sh by replacing curl-based IP detection with ifconfig -q or AWS metadata service, and add checksum verification before copying files.
MEDIUM: Add input validation to memory.js keys - reject special characters and only allow alphanumeric + underscore.
MEDIUM: Implement audit logging in session.js when JSON corruption is detected, rather than silently recovering.
LOW: Consider encrypting memory.json and session.json if they store authentication tokens or sensitive context.
LOW: Review all code correctly uses execFileSync instead of shell-based exec - this best practice is maintained throughout.
LOW: Add rate limiting and request logging to nginx.conf to detect abuse patterns.
